payload.probes:
FIVE ASSUMPTIONS PROBED AGAINST THE REAL CHANNEL. Two came back FALSE and change the design; one confirmed a predicted defect; two passed.

P1 - 'ripgrep will be available on the machine.' PROBE: `rg --version` on this machine (run-6405dc1414a2). RESULT: **FALSE** - 'Der Befehl rg ist entweder falsch geschrieben oder konnte nicht gefunden werden.' rg is NOT on PATH here, on the owner's own primary machine. CONSEQUENCE: the owner's reasoning at the kickoff - 'rg is gonna be available on all of them' - is true of rg as software but NOT of rg as an ambient command. So @vscode/ripgrep is not a convenience wrapper we could skip; it IS the delivery mechanism, and the whole no-fallback ruling rests on the npm package resolving rather than on any system install. RAID CONSEQUENCE: se.raid-rg-is-a-hard-dependency-with-no-fallback gets sharper - its trigger must be 'the PACKAGE fails to resolve a binary', not 'the machine lacks rg', and the documented-manual-install fallback is now the only fallback there is.

P2 - 'git grep can search a tag ref.' PROBE: `git grep -c "whitelist" iter/i8d-phone-brief -- "*.md"`. RESULT: **PASS**, and better than expected - it returned `iter/i8d-phone-brief:product/spec/ledger/se/law-whitelist-guards.md:1` and five more, in `ref:path:count` form. So R5's record search needs no new search engine at all: git already searches refs, and the output is parseable. This measurably shrinks the build.

P3 - 'the branch/tag name collision is real, not theoretical.' PROBE: the same call. RESULT: **CONFIRMED DEFECT** - git emitted `warning: refname 'iter/i8d-phone-brief' is ambiguous.` It resolved to one of them silently. So the record search would today be built on refs git itself calls ambiguous. R24 (delete the branch after close) is confirmed load-bearing rather than housekeeping, by observation rather than by argument.

P4 - 'v1 is reachable as a branch of this repository.' PROBE: `git grep -l "state of the art" main -- "product/quackitect/method/*"`. RESULT: **PASS** - returned `main:product/quackitect/method/prompts/engage.md`, `main:.../rigor/lean/checklist.md` and `main:.../rigor/systematic/checklist.md`. v1 is searchable with zero extra machinery, no declared root, no machine-local path. R6 and R7 shrink accordingly: declared roots stop being the critical path and remain only for genuinely external material. BONUS LEAD, recorded because it is exactly what this scan is for: v1's `engage.md` carries the research capability its checklist references, and I have not read it - a source for the M4 scan.

P5 - 'applies_to is machine-readable enough to join guidance onto packets.' PROBE: counted nodes carrying applies_to across the se ledger, and separately across machine-state nodes. RESULT: **FALSE, and this is the most consequential finding of the milestone.** Only TEN nodes in the entire ledger carry applies_to, and ZERO machine-state nodes do. Worse than the count: the field's CONTENT is free prose. My own laws written today say applies_to: 'every guard, check and refusal in the engine and in any design' and 'every hand-rolled script, ad-hoc command or out-of-lane edit'. Those are sentences for a human, not selectors a machine can match against a state id.

CONSEQUENCE OF P5, folded upstream now rather than discovered at build time: R14 as written - 'include every node whose applies_to matches that state' - is NOT IMPLEMENTABLE against today's data. The requirement stands, but its mechanism becomes an M4 decision with at least three candidates: (a) make applies_to machine-readable (state ids, state kinds, or tags) and migrate the ten existing nodes plus author it going forward; (b) have each state declare the rules it carries - rejected on sight, since that is exactly the hand-wiring whose absence caused the problem; (c) match semantically, reusing the BM25 index over applies_to text against the state's statement - cheap, already built, and fuzzy in a way that risks burying the instruction (se.raid-the-guidance-join-buries-the-instruction). This goes to enumerate_space as a real design question and, if (c) is a contender, to M5 as a spike, because 'does semantic matching pick the RIGHT laws for a state' is exactly the kind of claim that must be measured rather than assumed.

NOT PROBED, deliberately deferred to M5: whether the M4 element allocation is machine-readable enough for a models-adhered lint. It needs a prototype rather than a probe, and it was already named at gate_inputs as the one thing S2 rests on that is not yet known.
